root_cause.text: The vulnerability stems from an integer overflow in the size calculation within `rxgk_verify_response()` in the `rxrpc` subsystem, where relying on the rounded-up token length instead of the raw length allows the buffer bounds check to be bypassed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the condition in `net/rxrpc/rxgk.c` from `if (xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len)` to `if (token_len > len || xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len)`, and the CVE description explicitly states there is a "potential integer overflow due to rounding up token_len before checking it, thereby allowing the length check to be bypassed."

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs the buffer bounds check using xdr_round_up(token_len). According to the root cause, relying on the rounded-up token length instead of the raw length in this calculation allows an integer overflow that bypasses the security check. The rounding operation can cause the calculated size to exceed the actual allocated buffer size, enabling an attacker to craft malicious input that passes the bounds check while actually overflowing the buffer.
